statements.status_notes: The Marvin timing side-channel (RUSTSEC-2023-0071) affects RSA private-key operations (PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption/signing). The qdrant binary in this image is installed from the dhi/pkg-qdrant package (built with `cargo auditable build --release --locked --bin qdrant --features stacktrace`). rsa 0.9.10 is compiled in only transitively, via jsonwebtoken (rust_crypto feature) - jsonwebtoken is rsa's sole reverse-dependency in the lockfile. qdrant's JWT RBAC is locked to HS256 (HMAC-SHA256): src/common/auth/jwt_parser.rs:15 sets `const ALGORITHM = Algorithm::HS256` and validation is pinned to it, using the API key as a symmetric secret. Production code only verifies tokens (`decode()`); the sole `encode()` call is test-only (`#[cfg(test)]`) and also HMAC. qdrant never performs an RSA private-key operation, so the vulnerable code path is not in the shipped binary's execute path.

uv pulls in the rsa crate through Google service-account signing support. The advisory is for RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption; uv uses RSA signing for registry authentication workflows, matching existing uv VEX prior art.

RUSTSEC-2023-0071 ("Marvin Attack") is a timing side-channel in the rsa crate's RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 *decryption* path (RsaPrivateKey::decrypt, Pkcs1v15Encrypt). It does not affect the signature path. In the meilisearch v1.44.0 dependency tree, rsa@0.9.10 has exactly one consumer: jsonwebtoken@10.3.0. Inspection of jsonwebtoken's RSA module (src/crypto/rust_crypto/rsa.rs at v10.3.0) shows it imports only the signature-side surface — `Pkcs1v15Sign`, `Pss`, `RsaPublicKey`, `RsaPrivateKey`, and `pkcs1::{DecodeRsaPrivateKey, DecodeRsaPublicKey}` for key parsing — and exposes only `try_sign(msg)` and `verify(scheme, digest, signature)` operations to its callers. There is no import of `Pkcs1v15Encrypt`, no call to `RsaPrivateKey::decrypt`, and no RSA-decryption code reachable from any jsonwebtoken API. Meilisearch uses jsonwebtoken solely to mint and validate tenant-token JWTs (RS256/RS384/RS512/PS256/PS384/PS512), which are signing operations. The vulnerable decryption code in rsa@0.9.10 is therefore unreachable from the meilisearch binary.

uv pulls in the rsa crate via reqsign-google for RSA-PKCS1v15 signing of Google service-account JWTs (used when fetching Python packages from a GCS-backed index). RSA decryption, the only code path susceptible to the Marvin Attack timing oracle, is never exercised.
